send.title: ClientFrame
send.description:
Client to hub. The first frame must be `Auth` with a login token.

`{"type":"auth","token":"…","lock":true}`, `{"type":"call","id":1,"machine":"m1","call":{"cmd":"tabs"}}`,
`{"type":"hub","id":2,"call":{"cmd":"get_settings"}}`, `{"type":"attach","machine":"m1","tab":"tab-1"}`

lock.description:
The app asks for the password before a call only the account's owner makes
(`surface::owner_only`), so from now on the login alone, which the app keeps on disk,
runs none. An older app leaves it out and keeps every call it had.

unlock.description: The token `HubCall::Unlock` answered this app, sent again after a reconnect.

oneOf.description: Forwarded to the machine; the reply comes back as `ToClient::Reply` with this id.
Answered by the hub itself.
Streams the tab's output as `MachineEvent::Output`, starting with what its screen holds.

Call.description:
Everything a client may ask a machine to do, local or through the hub. The comment on each
variant names what `Machine::call` answers.

`{"cmd":"start_claude","tab":"tab-1","cols":120,"rows":32}`

oneOf.description: `Vec<TabView>`.
The new tab's id. `path: null` opens the machine's default folder.
The new tab's id, in the machine's folder for threads without a project.

Null. Whether the tab's session continues by itself once the usage limit that stopped it
lifts, which it does unless turned off.
The folder claude runs in. Restarts claude when it is already running.

Null. The tab is on the client's screen: a session that sleeps starts at this size, and
one that runs stays awake. The client sends it again while the tab stays there.

The folder claude runs in. Restarts claude with `bypass` turned `on` or off, resuming the
tab's conversation; a session already running that way is left alone.

The folder claude runs in. Restarts claude on the tab's conversation with `--model model`,
which picks it for that conversation alone. With `account`, moves the conversation to that
account first when it is another one, so a model from another provider keeps the thread.

The folder claude runs in. Restarts claude on the tab's conversation, so its skills,
plugins and MCP servers load again.
`null`. Keystrokes as xterm reports them.
`null`.
`null`.

`null`, once the tab's turn is stopped as the app's Stop button stops it: claude's background
agents and workflows first, then the turn, then the turn their "stopped" notices wake.

`null`, once `reply` closes the questionnaire `id` open on the tab. Refused when it is
closed already, or the reply does not fit its questions.

The tab's new folder, canonical. Stands in for the folder dialog on a remote machine;
the client then sends `StartClaude`.
`Vec<ProjectView>`, most recent first.
`Vec<history::Turn>`, newest first, only `session`'s when given.
The folder's `origin` remote, or `null`.
`projects::Folders`: the subfolders matching a path as typed so far, such as `~/pro`.

`scaffold::Created`: a new folder named after `name` in `~/pinned`, a git repository with
a first commit, opened as a project.
The URL of the private GitHub repository the project at `path` is now pushed to.

The folder of a clone of `repo`, found among the machine's projects or cloned into `~/pinned`,
or cloned into `dest` when given, which must not hold files yet.
The hub adds the account's GitHub token, for a private repository.
The folder `path`, canonical, made first with its parents when it doesn't exist.
`Vec<ThreadMatch>`: the tabs whose conversations hold `query`, prompts' matches first.
The new tab's id, with claude already running. Refused when the folder can't be found or cloned.

The new tab's id, as `Run` makes it, but not started: the hub reopens an archived conversation
for an agent this way, which then starts it with `start_claude`, under the limits.

The new tab's id, with claude already running, for a workflow's Run now: a task held to the
limits of the project it runs in, whose first finished turn ends it and goes to the
delegation metrics. Refused past the limits. Only the hub sends it, for `run_workflow`;
inside `ActFor` the asking session's own task narrows the limits and hears when it ends.
`true` when a live tab whose environment holds every pair took `text` as a prompt.

The absolute path the file was saved under, in a private folder of the machine, for a
session to read. Refused past `uploads::LIMIT`.

The `data:` URL of an image upload at `path`, so a chat draws it from any machine. Refused
outside the uploads folder, for a file that isn't a picture, and past 8 MB.

The `data:` URL of the picture file at `path`, so a chat draws a picture a reply names by
path. `path` is absolute or starts with `~/`. Refused otherwise, for a file that isn't a
picture, and past 8 MB.
`Vec<accounts::View>`: the built-in accounts, then the added ones, each as its CLI reports it.

`Vec<claude_models::ClaudeModel>`: Claude's models after keeping the rows of claude's
/model menu that `lines`, a tab's screen, shows. Refused when the menu isn't on it.

The new account's `accounts::View`. Its id is a slug of `name`. `auth` is `opencode-go`
when `key` is an OpenCode Go API key.
The account's `accounts::View`. Refused for an account that signs in with a CLI login.
`null`. Projects that ran under it fall back to the default account.
The project's `ProjectView`. `account: null` runs it under the default account again.
The id of the project's orchestrator tab: the one already open, else a new one, not yet started.

`global_orchestrator::Handoff`. Hands `text` to the Capitão of the project at `path`,
opening it when missing, as `[<sender>] <text>`: typed now when it is idle, its first prompt
when it is stopped, else queued until it is idle, or refused as busy when `busy` (else this
machine's setting) says so. A repeat of `request_id` answers the first outcome and types nothing.

sender.description: The orchestrator's name; blank takes this machine's.

oneOf.description:
`global_orchestrator::Handoff`. Hands a Capitão's report to this machine's global
orchestrator, opening it when missing, as `CaptainReport::line`. It never refuses as busy. A
repeat of `request_id` answers the first outcome and types nothing.

The id of this machine's global orchestrator tab: the one already open, else a new one, not
yet started, in `~/.pinned/orquestrador`, made when missing and never listed as a project.

The id of a new tab, not yet started, whose session adjusts `scope`'s way of working with
the taste tools and whose first prompt says so. It opens in the project folder `path`, or
in the folder for threads without a project.

The started task's JSON, as `delegate_task` answers it. From the hub: starts a worker
thread here for a tab on another machine of the account. `origin.machine` is the hub's
stamp of the machine that asked; the thread nests under `origin.tab` there. `repo` names
the checkout it works in, cloned with `token` when this machine has none. A repeat of
`origin.task` answers the task it started.

The task's status JSON, as `task_status` answers it, or its state once cancelled when
`cancel` gives a reason. From the hub: only for the task `Delegate` started for `tab` and
`task` of `origin_machine`, the hub's stamp of the machine that asks.

`null`. From the hub: the task this machine's tab `tab` sent to `from` with `delegate_task`
ended there. `from` is the hub's stamp of the machine that reports it.

`null`. From the hub: the worker of the task this machine's tab `tab` sent to `from` waits
on the user for `ask`, or, with none, waits on nothing now.
`global_orchestrator::Settings` of this machine.
The `global_orchestrator::Settings` saved, with a blank name back to the default one.
`auto_archive::Settings` of this machine: when it archives a finished session.
The `auto_archive::Settings` saved, answered as saved.

`on`, as saved. Whether the desktop app on this machine runs in the background, with no
window, which it applies at once: on closes the window, off opens it. A machine without the
app refuses it.

`reading::read` of the tab's session: its state and the last `items` items of its
conversation, 20 when not given, read from the end of its transcript however long it is.

`repo_look::look` of the checkout at `path`, a project folder of this machine: read-only,
with secrets left out. The global orchestrator's repo tools, sent by the hub.

`Vec<memory::Memory>`: the project's memories that best match `query`, best first, or the
latest ones for an empty query.

The `memory::Memory` saved. With `id`, replaces that memory. Refused when the project
already has a memory with the same title or nearly the same meaning.
The `memory::Memory` removed.
`memory::Status`: how many memories the project has and whether search also matches by meaning.
The new tab's id, running the CLI's login for the account in the account's home.

The long-lived token `claude setup-token` prints for the Claude account `account`, which the
user approves in the browser it opens on this machine. It runs in no tab, and the machine
answers it only to the hub, which keeps it for that account's boxes.
Whether a `SetupToken` for `account` was waiting, which this stops.

The tab's folder, as `start_claude`. Moves the tab's conversation to another Claude Code
account signed in here and resumes it there, continuing a turn a usage limit stopped.

`ThreadPage`: the conversation's items from byte `from` of its transcript on. With `limit`,
the newest whole turns holding at least `limit` items before byte `before` instead, or
before the end, read back from there; `from` is then unused and the page's `start` is the
`before` of the page older than it.
`null`. Types `text` into the session as one prompt and submits it.
`workspace::Workspace` of the tab's folder.
What `gh pr view` answers for `pr`, a number or URL, run in the tab's folder, plus `diff`.
`workspace::PrStatus`: whether `pr` is open, a draft, merged or closed, without its diff.
`Option<String>`: the icon of the tab's project, where T3 Code looks for one, as a data URL.

`String`: a new title for the tab's conversation, which `claude -p` writes from `thread`, its
messages, and the `previous` title. An empty `thread` reads the tab's own conversation.
What `gh pr list` answers in the tab's folder: number, title, state, isDraft, url, headRefName.
`null`. Merges `pr`, or marks it ready, through gh in the tab's folder.
`workspace::Diff`: the tab's working tree against HEAD or the default branch.

base.description: The branch `DiffScope::Base` compares with, instead of the default one.

oneOf.description: `Vec<workspace::Listener>`: the machine's web servers, the tab's session's own first.
`Vec<workspace::Editor>` installed on the machine.
`Vec<commands::Command>`, the slash commands claude offers in the tab's folder.
`Vec<String>`: the tab's folder's files and folders, relative, for `@` mentions.
`skills::Listing`: every skill folder on the machine.
`skills::SkillText` of `file` in the listed skill folder at `dir`.

`skills::SaveReport`. Writes `text` to `file` in each listed, writable copy that is
unchanged since its `since`, then reloads the sessions that load them.
`branches::Branches` of the tab's folder.
`null`. Switches the tab's folder to `branch`, a new one when `create`. Refused while claude works there.

from.description: Makes or resets `branch` at this ref instead, fetched first when it is `origin/…`.

oneOf.description: `pulls::PullRequests` of the GitHub repositories of the machine's folders `paths`, through gh.

limit.description: Rows per search at most; the page asks for more 100 at a time.

oneOf.description: `pulls::Stack` the pull request `number` of github.com's `repo` (`owner/name`) sits in, or `null`.
`pulls::FilterOptions` of `kind` matching `query` in the GitHub repositories of the folders `paths`.
`Vec<pulls::FileStat>` of pull request `number` of `repo` on `host`, or `null` when it changes too many files.

`Vec<usage::Row>`: the tokens claude's transcripts on the machine record from unix time `since`
on, priced with the machine's `usage::PriceBook` over LiteLLM's list.
`usage::PriceBook`: the prices and model mappings the user set on the machine.
The `usage::PriceBook` after setting each model's price and mapping, or clearing it with `null`.
`usage::Limits`: the account and plan limits claude's own usage check reports.
`panel::PageMeta` of the web page at `url`, fetched from this machine.

frame_by.description:
The origin of the page that would frame it, when a web app asks. A policy that names that
origin lets the page through.

oneOf.description: `panel::Refs`: the tab's folder's local and remote branches, for picking what to compare with.

What a step of the header's Git action answers: a commit message, a pull request URL, or
`null`. Refused while claude works in the tab's folder.
`scripts::ProjectScripts` of the tab's project.
`null`. Replaces the scripts of the tab's project.
`null`. Checks out the pull request `pr`, a number or URL, in the tab's folder with gh. Refused while claude works there.

The tab's new folder. Moves a tab whose conversation hasn't begun to a worktree of its
project, `"new"` for one made from what it has checked out, or a path, or back to the
project's own checkout with `null`, and restarts claude there. Refused while claude works.
`panel::FileText` of `path` in the tab's folder, or in its repository when `root`, as of `rev` when given.

The tab's watched pull request URLs, after starting or stopping the watch on `pr` when given.
A watched pull request wakes the tab's claude when its checks finish, someone comments, or
its branch starts to conflict.

A loopback URL that serves `path` with the folder around it, for a page that loads its own
styles and scripts.
The saved file's new hash. Refused when the file changed since the read that answered `since`.
`Vec<panel::Hit>`: the lines of the tab's folder that hold `query`.
`null`. Retitles `pr` or rewrites its description.
`null`. Comments on `pr`, or answers its review thread `reply_to`.
`null`. Submits a review of `pr` with its line comments.
`null`. Runs the check at `check`, a GitHub Actions link, again.
`{guide, run}`: the review guide kept for `pr` and the run writing one. `write` starts a run.

`null`. Reacts on `pr` or a remark on it, rewrites a comment, asks for or takes back a
review, puts a label on or off, or resolves a review thread.
`{candidates, truncated}`: who `pr` may ask for a review, or the labels it may carry.

`null`. Merges `pr` and the stack layers under it, or rebases its whole GitHub stack, if every
unmerged layer still has the head in `heads`.

The id of a new login shell in the tab's folder, which `attach`, `write_input`, `resize_pty`
and `close_shell` take as a tab id.
`null`. Ends the shell `shell`.
`Vec<String>`: those of `shells` running a command, as T3 Code's terminal-running pulse reads them.

The address of the machine's device hub, which mirrors its simulators and emulators. It
starts on the first call; `embed` is the origin of a page that frames it.

Whether new sessions may drive the machine's simulators and emulators, after setting it to
`allow` when given.

What `op` answers, run against the machine's device hub, which starts first when it isn't
running, and its simulator and emulator tools.
`Devices`.

The opened device's id, an Android emulator's serial once it runs. Boots it when it is off,
and attaches the hub's stream to an iOS simulator.
`null`. Powers the device off.
A `data:image/png` URL of the screen.

`null`. An Android gesture, key or text in the hub's socket shape, for a page that can't open
the socket itself.
The hub's accessibility tree, as the platform's helper answers it.
`Detail`: the settings T3's tools panel shows, and the app in front.
`null`. Changes a setting or acts on an app.
`Vec<thread::Item>`: the conversation of the subagent the tab's `Agent` tool call `tool` started.

The folder claude runs in. Restarts the tab's claude on a copy of its conversation that stops before
the prompt `before`, after putting the folder's files back as they were then when `files`.

The new tab's id, not yet started: its claude resumes a copy of the tab's conversation through
the message `through`.
The path saved, relative to the tab's folder. Writes `text` to `path` inside that folder.
The new tab's id, not yet started: it resumes the delegated task's conversation in the child's folder.
The task_status body. Stops the delegated task when this tab owns it.
`null`. Types that finished task's notice into the tab now. The tab must own the task.
`null`. The tabs whose transcript changes this caller hears of as `MachineEvent::Thread`. Empty asks for none.
The machine's `UpdateStatus`.
Why the machine stopped syncing projects and plugins, or `null` while it syncs.

`load::MachineState`: the machine's load and accounts now, which the hub asks for before it
refuses a delegation on what the machine reported earlier.

`null`. Sets an unreadable sync state aside, so the next sync starts over as on a new
machine. A readable one is left alone.

What `call`, a `Call` as JSON, answers when run for the agent session in tab `caller` on this
machine, as the hub passes on that session's `act`. A call that starts a session holds it to
the caller's delegation limits (`surface::Action::starts_work`).

`true` once `text` is queued for the tab, as worker reports are: typed once its session is
idle. A `tab` gone since, as after a restart, is found by its Claude `session`. `false` when
no tab has it. A repeat of `id` queues nothing.

`Vec<mcp::Server>`: the MCP servers Claude Code sessions here load under `account`, else the
account of the project at `path`, else the default one. User and local scope come from that
account's `.claude.json`, project scope from `path`'s `.mcp.json`. Each names its program or
its URL's origin only, never its arguments, environment or headers.

`Vec<mcp::Found>`: the servers `McpServers` lists, with their command, arguments and URL and
the names of their environment and headers, never their values, for the app to import.

QuestionsReply.description:
How the user closed a questionnaire.

`{"kind":"answered","answers":[{"chosen":["main"]}]}`, `{"kind":"skipped"}`

oneOf.description: One answer per question, in the questions' order.
The agent goes on with its recommendations and states its assumptions.

Answer.description: The answer to one question: the labels of the options chosen, what the user typed, or both.

RunSpec.description:
A connector's session, the same on any machine.

`{"folder":"/repo","repo":"git@github.com:o/r.git","args":["--name","ENG-7"],"env":[["PINNED_CONNECTOR","c1"]]}`

folder.description: The folder on the machine the connector was set up on.

repo.description: The folder's git origin, which finds or clones it on a machine without that folder.

args.description: `claude` arguments, with `EXE_PLACEHOLDER` where the pinned binary goes.

token.description: The account's GitHub token, added by the hub, which clones a private repository.

account.description: The agent account the connector names; none runs the session under its project's.

budget_usd.description: What may be spent on the box running this, in USD; none leaves the hub's lifetime cap.

Provider.description:
One row per agent CLI pinned can host. A table, so adding a provider is one entry, not a
branch per call site.

Auth.description: How an account signs in. An account written before this field existed is a CLI login.

BusyPolicy.description: What happens to a message for a Capitão that is busy.

oneOf.description: It waits in the Capitão's queue and is typed once the Capitão is idle.
It is refused with `ocupado`, and the orchestrator tries again later.

CaptainReport.description:
What a Capitão tells the global orchestrator, at the end of a turn one of its messages started
or through `tell_orchestrator`.

machine.description: The machine the Capitão runs on. Empty when that machine does not know its id.

project.description: The project's name, its folder's.

path.description: The project's folder on that machine.

answers.description:
The `request_id`s of the orchestrator's messages whose turn this report ends. Empty for
`tell_orchestrator`.

oneOf.description: The global orchestrator.
Every project's Capitão.
One project's Capitão, by its repo as in `github.com/acme/site`.

Origin.description:
The tab on another machine that delegated a task here. The hub stamps `machine` from the
socket the request came on.

task.description: The caller's own id for the task, which the end notice names.

access.description: The widest access the caller may hand a child.

delegator.description: Who asked, for the record this machine keeps of the task it runs.

limits.description: The delegation limits the caller runs under, which the worker here is held to.

Access.description:
What the child is allowed to do. Never wider than the parent tab: plan narrows a bypassed
parent to read-only, and a parent that asks before acting does not hand the child a bypass.

Delegator.description: The session that started a task.

project.description: The project's repo (`host/owner/name`), else its folder.

oneOf.description: A thread with no role: the user's own session.

Limits.description: A scope's delegation limits, resolved: what `delegate_task` and the boxes enforce.

Cost.description: What a model costs to run, coarsely: routing by tier beats stale per-token prices.

oneOf.description: Haiku and flash models: sweeps, translations, first drafts.
The middle default when nothing is known.
Opus and max efforts: architecture and hairy bugs.

Effort.description: How hard a model thinks, from least to most, as `orchestrator_capabilities` names the levels.

Request.description: The delegation request, after the MCP arguments have been read once.

budget_ms.description: As asked; `run_limits` settles both under the caller's time limit.

tools.description:
Tools the child may use. The child sees them as its grant; empty grants what the task
needs. A child that needs more says NEEDS followed by the tools, and the parent answers
with a wider grant.

heavy.description: Whether the account's placement policy places this worker, over its rule for heavy work.

driver_kind.description: Set when the request named `driverKind`, so a custom account can be checked against it.

machine.description: Another machine of the account, by id or name, that runs the child.

box.description: A new Upstash Box, opened with the account's connection on the hub, that runs the child.

size.description: None follows the project's and the account's default box size when the box opens.

repo.description: The repository the box clones. None clones the caller's.

Interaction.description: `plan` is read-only. `inherit` and `default` leave the parent's mode alone.

RuntimeMode.description: How wide a child may act. Omitted means the parent's own mode.

RemoteEnd.description: How a task that runs on another machine ended, as that machine reports it.

state.description: `result_available`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

usage.description:
What the worker used, its box's time included: the delegating task shows it. An older
machine sends none. The machine that ran the task records the run, so this is for display.

TaskUsage.description: What a delegated worker has used so far. The limits enforce `cost_usd`; the metrics keep the rest.

tokens_in.description: Input tokens, cache reads and cache writes included.

cost_usd.description: The tokens priced as the Usage page prices them. None while a model the worker used has no price.

box_usd.description: What the worker's Upstash Box cost, for box work.

box_ms.description: The box time `box_usd` pays for: since the box's previous task ended, or since it was made.

RemoteAsk.description:
What a task that runs on another machine waits on the user for: its thread there is blocked on
an approval or a question. The machine that runs it reports it as it starts and again, as `None`,
once it is answered, and the thread that delegated the task keeps it until then.

tool.description: The tool an approval is for, such as `Bash`.

ask.description: What the thread asks, as its session said it.

since.description: Unix seconds the thread started to wait.

AskKind.description: What a session that cannot go on without the user asks of them.

oneOf.description: A tool waits on a permission prompt.
The session asked a question (`AskUserQuestion`).

GlobalOrchestratorSettings.description: How this machine's global orchestrator works. One file in the machine's config folder.

name.description: The chat's name, and the prefix of every message it hands a Capitão, as in `[Orchestrator] `.

host.description: This machine hosts the account's global orchestrator. One machine of the account does.

group_reports.description: The chat folds consecutive reports into one row.

read_aloud.description: The phone reads the orchestrator's summaries aloud.

ReportPolicy.description: When a Capitão reports to the global orchestrator.

oneOf.description: At the end of every turn that a message from the orchestrator started, and with `tell_orchestrator`.
Only with `tell_orchestrator`.

AutoArchiveSettings.description: When this machine archives a finished session. A grace period is in minutes, and null is never.

workers.description: Worker threads, the tabs a `delegate_task` started.

sessions.description: Every other session, the ones the user opened.

RepoLook.description: What the global orchestrator asks of a checkout.

oneOf.description:
Its shape: HEAD, size, languages, top folders, packages, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the
start of the README, and the latest commits.
`lines` lines of `file` from `from_line` (1 when not given), at `rev` when given.

Lines that hold `query`, in files that match `glob` when given; with `glob` alone, the
tracked paths that match it.
Marks a draft ready for review.
Turns an open pull request back into a draft.
Opens a pull request that undoes this merged one.
Merges once the required checks and reviews pass, by the method named.
Deletes a merged pull request's branch on GitHub.
The working tree, untracked files too, against HEAD.
The working tree against where HEAD left the default branch.

Target2.description: One copy a save should write, with the tree the client read it at.

Filters.description: T3 Code's list filters, each one of GitHub's search qualifiers.

labels.description: A row holds a label of every group; a group's names are GitHub's own OR.

Price.description: A price the user set for a model, in USD per million tokens; cache prices left out are input's.

GitStep.description: One step of the header's Git action, which the page runs in order to show where it is.

oneOf.description: A commit message for `files`, or every change, written by a headless claude.
Commits `files`, or every change, with `message`.
Pushes the branch, setting its upstream on `origin` the first time.
Opens a pull request of the branch with gh, titled and described from its commits.
Fast-forwards the branch to its upstream.
Makes the folder a git repository.
Creates `name` on GitHub with gh, as `origin`, and pushes to it.

runOnWorktreeCreate.description: Runs in a new worktree as it is made for a thread.

async.description: With `run_on_worktree_create`, claude starts only once the script exits.

runOnSettle.description: Runs in a thread's worktree when the thread settles.

side.description: `RIGHT` for the new side, `LEFT` for a removed line.

PrChange.description: A change to who is on a pull request, what is on it, and its review threads.

oneOf.description: Adds or takes back the viewer's `content` on `subject`, a comment, review or the pull request.
Asks `login`, a person or a team's `org/slug`, for a review, or takes the request back.
Resolves the review thread `thread`, or opens it again.
Rewrites the comment `id`, a remark on the pull request or, with `review`, on a line.

Reaction.description: GitHub's reactions, by the name its GraphQL API gives them.

oneOf.description: Merges the pull request and the unmerged layers under it, as GitHub's merge-async does.
Rebases every unmerged layer, bottom to top, onto the stack's base.

StackHead.description: A layer's head as the reader last saw it, so a stack that moved since is not acted on.

HubCall.description:
Account-level calls, answered by the hub. Names and arguments match the app's Tauri
commands, so the settings page sends either. The last three come only from machines,
forwarding a connector session's callbacks to the hub, which holds the keys.

`{"cmd":"connect_linear","key":"lin_api_…"}`, `{"cmd":"stage","connector":"c1","issue":"uuid","stage":"coding"}`

oneOf.description: `connectors::Settings`.
`linear::Account`.
`connectors::Suggestions`.
`slack::Connected`: `slack::Account` with the bot and whether the token added it.

bot.description: The bot to remove; empty for the default bot, which is what an app before several bots means.

oneOf.description: Channel names.

bot.description: The bot whose channels to list; empty for the default bot.

oneOf.description: `github::Account`.
`Vec<github::Repo>`, most recently pushed first.
`vercel::Account`, once the gateway took the key.
`Vec<vercel::Model>`: chat models tagged `structured-output`, and every decision model. The list needs no key.
`upstash::Account`, once Upstash took the key. Only a signed-in app runs boxes, so this has no Tauri command.

From a machine: the latest replies of the Capitão of the project at `path` on `machine`, as
`reading::read` answers them, with `project` set to `path`.

`taste::Tastes`: the account's, or the defaults while it has none. A machine asks too, when it

`taste::Tastes`, once `field` of `scope` is back to what it inherits.
From a machine: `true` when the account had no tastes and took these, a signed-out app's own.

`taste::BoxSizeChoice`: the size a box cloning `repo` opens at when its call names `size`,
or none, and which setting chose it. Without `repo`, a box of no project: the account's.

`taste::Tastes`, once the default box size of `repo`'s project, or the account's without
`repo`, is `size`. No `size` clears it: the project inherits the account's again, and the
account's goes back to the built-in small.

From the machine that hosts the global orchestrator, for its tab `tab`: `Call::RepoLook` of
`project` (a key `projects` lists) on `machine`, an id or a name, else on the checkout a
Capitão runs in, the asking machine's own, or the first online one; with `machine`,

From a machine: `Call::ReadSession` of the tab `tab` on `machine`, an id or a name, else on
the online machine that has that tab, with `id`, `machine` and `machine_name` set.

From a machine: the started task's JSON. Runs `request` on the machine or in the Upstash Box
its target names, for the asking machine's tab `tab`, whose own id for the task is `task`.
`repo` is the caller's git origin, which the worker's checkout is found or cloned by;
`access` is the widest the caller may hand a child; `delegator` and `limits` are who asked
and the limits it runs under, which the worker is held to and recorded with.

From a machine: the status JSON of the task its tab `tab` delegated to `machine` as `task`,
or its state once cancelled when `cancel` gives a reason.

From a machine: `null` once machine `to` took the end of the task its tab `tab` delegated
here as `task`.

From a machine: `true` once machine `to` took what the worker of the task its tab `tab`
delegated here as `task` waits on the user for. No `ask` says it waits on nothing now.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`. Keeps `token`, a `claude setup-token` token, for

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, without the token kept for `name`.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, once `machine` ran `claude setup-token` for its
Claude account `account` and the hub kept the token it printed under that name. The token

Whether `machine` was still waiting on a `MintBoxClaudeToken` for `account`, which this stops.

From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps these records of its delegated tasks, as they
are now. The hub stamps the machine, and box time for a machine that is a box.

`delegate::DelegationStats` of the account's delegated tasks that ended in the last `days`
(1, 7 or 30), on every machine.

`Vec<delegate::UnclaimedEnd>`: the account's worker ends that the machine whose tab delegated
the task answered it did not take, as a machine that restarted and forgot the task does.
The hub keeps each for 30 days, newest first.

`upstash::BoxUsage`: the account's Upstash Box usage, and pinned's count of the box time its
delegated tasks used this UTC month. The Upstash key stays on the hub.

`Vec<upstash::StuckBox>`: the account's boxes pinned could not delete, with why, from the
hub's own record and rows. It reads no Upstash key and calls no Upstash.
`Vec<marks::SessionMarks>`: how the user filed each of the account's conversations.

landed in order. One left with only its id has no mark. The account's clients hear the same

`marks::SessionMarks` of the conversation in `tab`, once it is archived as `ArchiveSession`

`Target`: the new tab, on the archived conversation's machine, that resumes it with its name
and pin back.

`null`, once the conversation's tab closed and its marks are gone, so pinned forgets it.
Claude Code keeps its transcript.

asked; either way the session gets a notice. `entered` holds what the user typed in the app

`Vec<surface::AuditEntry>`: the account's audit trail of agents' acts, newest first, `limit`

`Vec<mcp::Entry>`: the account's own MCP servers, which every session pinned starts loads

BoxAccess.description: The account's choice for each kind of actor.

Project.description: A project of the account, offered on machines that don't have it yet.

repo.description: The origin as the machine that shared it has it, which clones it elsewhere.

size.description: Compressed bytes.

executable.description: Unix mode when the sender read one. Absent when the sender does not know the mode.

Sets the executable bit on a file the hub already stores, without sending bytes.
The hub applies it only while that file's sha is still `sha`.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; empty keeps claude's default.

worktree.description: Runs each session in its own git worktree, so parallel issues don't share a checkout.

since.description:
Only issues created after this instant (RFC 3339) trigger, so saving a connector
doesn't start sessions for the backlog. Slack connectors move it forward on every check.

handled.description: Issues, or Slack threads as `<channel id>:<thread ts>`, that already started a session.

team.description: The Linear team a Slack connector's sessions file issues in, by name or key.

label.description: The Linear label put on the issues a Slack connector's sessions file; empty puts none.

fix.description: Whether a Slack connector's sessions may file a Linear issue and fix the bug.

created.description: The issue each Slack thread's session filed, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

followed.description: How far each handled Slack thread was passed on to its session, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

proof.description: Whether a session that opens a pull request must prove it works, with a Playwright video.

ask.description: Asks a gateway model about the trigger's find before the session starts. None skips it.

account.description: The account its sessions run under; empty runs them under their project's.

slackBot.description:
The id of the Slack bot that watches and answers for it; empty is the default bot. A called
workflow answers with the bot of the thread it was handed instead.

graph.description:
The workflow drawn as a graph. None runs the fixed pipeline the fields above describe.
Older apps neither send nor read it.

oneOf.description: A Linear issue created with this label.
A Slack message in this channel, by name or id, that mentions the bot.

Every new message people start in this channel, by name or id, which a decision model sorts
into one of `decide`'s categories. The workflow has no session of its own.

A Slack thread a message workflow's category hands it, which its session answers as a
mention's session would. It watches no channel of its own.

model.description: A decision model on the Vercel AI Gateway, such as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

fallback.description: The category, by name, that takes a message the model is unsure about. None keeps its guess.

at the category.

Columns.description: The Linear column each stage moves the issue to. Empty leaves the issue where it is.

Fix.description: How far a Slack connector's session goes with a bug it finds.

oneOf.description: Analyze and reply; never file an issue or change code.
Analyze, then ask in the thread; file and fix only once someone answered it with a mention.
Fix obvious bugs right away, and ask about the rest.

cursor.description: The newest message the session has seen, as a Slack ts.

seen.description: The newest message pinned read, when people wrote past `cursor` without mentioning the bot.

replied.description: Someone mentioned the bot in the thread after its session started, which `Fix::Ask` waits for.

Ask.description: A model on Vercel's AI Gateway that reads what the trigger found before the session starts.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`. The id picks chat or decision when the step runs.

name.description: The key the answer goes under, as `kind`.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text.

stopOn.description: Choices that end the workflow without a session.

id string ("" = any), or `{"kind":"upstash-box",…}`. Old stores load as before, and an old UI
that never touches the select saves the object back untouched.

size.description:
Left out when the workflow names none. A workflow saved before the default box size
always has one, since the old app wrote its default, medium, out.

edges.description: Order matters: a port's edges run in this order, each branch to its end before the next.

Node.description:
Everything a node can be. The session can also do most of these through `pinned` callbacks;
when both a node and the session post the same reply or file the same issue, the second write
is skipped, whichever runs first. Coding and review moves named in the connector's `columns`
stay implicit prompt instructions, alongside any `move-column` step.

Slack follow-ups in the thread are not a node. While the run's session is open, new thread
messages are typed into it, as today.

position.description: Canvas pixels of the node's center. The editor owns them.

group_name.description: The named group box the editor draws this node in. The runner ignores it.

oneOf.description: What starts a run. The walk begins at its outgoing edges.
One Vercel AI Gateway call that answers every question, and branches on one of them.
Branches on an answer an earlier classify already gave. No model call.

Tells the run's one Claude session something. The first `talk` of a run opens the session
with the session owner's settings; every later one, on any branch, types into it.

Opens the run's session with this step's own setup, then works like `talk`: the first
`session` of a run opens it, every later one types into it. Empty text fields inherit the
session owner's settings, so a bare node behaves exactly like `talk`.
Pings a Slack user group, by handle or id, in the run's thread.
Moves the Linear issue to the connector's `picked` column, as opening a session does today.

Posts `text` in the run's Slack thread, hub-side. A second post of the same text in the
same run is skipped, whether the node or the session posts first.

Files a Linear issue for the run's Slack thread, hub-side, linking back to the thread.
An issue the thread already filed is answered, never filed twice.

Works the run's Slack thread on an existing issue: the named identifier, or the issue
the thread already filed when empty.
Moves the run's Linear issue to the named column.

Requires a proof video on the pull request: like the connector's proof flag, it appends
the proof instructions to the session's opening prompt. The session still records the video.

Lets the run's session read the Convex deployment `connection` names: every table, or only
`tables`, which also turns off queries and logs. Like `proof`, it counts anywhere in the
workflow's own graph, and it adds a note to the session's opening prompt.
Walks another connector's graph inside this run, with this run's session.
Ends this branch on purpose. A port with no edge also ends its branch.

Watch.description: The trigger kinds, without the routing a fixed-pipeline `SlackMessage` carried in `Decide`.

oneOf.description: Runs only when another graph `call`s it.

name.description: The key the answer goes under in the run's context.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text and cannot be branched on.

description.description: What the model reads to tell this choice from the others.

PortId.description: A choice's stable id, or one of the fixed ports below. Reordering or renaming choices keeps edges.

oneOf.description: The port is the model's choice.

Today's `Decide::pick`: below `unsure_below` the fallback takes it, and below `page_at` a
choice whose branch pages a group gives way to the likeliest quiet one, or to `nowhere`.
An unsure answer keeps the model's guess.
An unsure answer takes this existing choice's port, as a `Decide` fallback category does.
An unsure answer takes an extra `fallback` port.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

branchOn.description: The name of the question whose choices are the ports. None leaves one `out` port.

Switch.description: Reads one answer from `classify` and takes the first case that matches, ignoring ASCII case.

cases.description: In order. The first `equals` that matches the answer wins.

SessionSetup.description:
The session setup a `session` step carries. Empty text fields inherit the session owner's
own session settings; `worktree` set here opens a separate worktree even when the owner would
share the checkout.

prompt.description: What this step tells the session, appended to the owner's opening prompt on open.

folder.description: The folder the session opens in; empty inherits the owner's.

repo.description: The repository a machine without the folder clones; empty inherits the owner's.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; empty keeps the owner's model.

effort.description: low, medium, high, xhigh or max; empty inherits the owner's effort.

permission.description: manual, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions or plan; empty inherits.

account.description: The account id its session runs under; empty runs the project's account.

worktree.description: Whether the session gets its own git worktree.

instructions.description: Instructions sent before the subject; empty inherits the owner's.

tz.description: IANA name, as `America/Sao_Paulo`; set from the creator's device.

grace_mins.description: Minutes after `due_at` during which a run still counts as on time. None = [`DEFAULT_GRACE_MINS`].

on_missed.description: What to do with a run that was not delivered within grace. None = `OnMissed::default_for(schedule)`.

pickup_mins.description: Minutes a delivered run may wait for its target to start it. None = [`DEFAULT_PICKUP_MINS`].

fyi.description:
Hub-computed, read-only: when an agent created the task and the user has not looked yet. The
Inbox shows a row for it. Unix seconds.

oneOf.description: A wall-clock date and time in the task's zone: `2026-11-13T09:00`.
Five-field cron, evaluated in the task's zone.
The user: a notification on every device, with no agent run.
The global Orchestrator, on the machine that hosts it.
A project's Captain, by repo key; an empty machine means wherever `send_to_captain` would pick.
An existing conversation, by Claude session id, so it survives tab restarts.
A new worker in a project, placed like `delegate_task`.
Text the target receives as one prompt.
Run now of a saved workflow. The target is ignored: the workflow's own `runs_on` decides.
The run becomes `missed` and the user decides: Run now or Skip.
Record the run as `skipped`; the next occurrence comes as usual.
Run as soon as a path opens, whenever that is.

NeverItem.description: The items of the never list, in the order of the design's table.

Fallback2.description: Where a run goes when its target's machine is not there.

oneOf.description: Wait within the grace window. A box costs money, so this is the default.
Open a box, for the targets that allow it.

Actor.description: Who created a task or an idea: the user, or an agent by the part it plays.

ActorRole.description: The part the session that acted plays, as its tab shows it.

Need.description: What a worker needs from the machine that runs it.

Stage.description: Where a connector's session is in its work on an issue. Each stage maps to a Linear column.

oneOf.description: The harness picked the issue up and opened a session for it.
The session is about to change code.
The session opened the pull request.

AgentProject.description: A project an external agent may work in: one folder on one machine.

RelayTo.description: Where a relayed message goes, and what it carries.

oneOf.description:
`text` for the Capitão of the project at `path` on `machine`, as `Call::Enqueue` takes it.
The hub takes it only from the machine that hosts the account's global orchestrator.

hub takes it only from a machine whose Capitão tab `report.tab` works in `report.path`.

`text` for the Capitão of `repo` in an Upstash Box the hub opens with the account's own
connection, or the box that already runs it. Taken only from the global orchestrator's host.

A project's box size over the account's. A patch can set it but not clear it; resetting
the field clears it.

placement.description:
The account's placement policy. Only the Captains' and the orchestrator's scope take it:
it belongs to the account, and a project's own comes later.

Strategy.description: How a worker climbs the model ladder.

oneOf.description: The cheapest rung with a detailed brief, re-briefed narrower before it moves up.
The cheapest rung, one rung up after two failures.
The hard model from the start.

ModelRef.description: A model as `orchestrator_capabilities` names it, and the provider it runs through when that matters.

Autonomy.description: What the agents decide without the user.

Placement.description: An account's placement policy, in Settings › Way of working.

avoid.description:
Machine ids never chosen by rank. One runs a worker only as the machine that asked, when
nothing else fits.

oneOf.description:
Workers with `isolation: "worktree"`. A shared worker works in the caller's checkout, and
another machine would not see its uncommitted changes.

TasteField.description: One knob of a `Taste`, named as its JSON field.

projects.description: Each project's changes over `captains`, by repo.

placement.description: Where the account's heavy delegated work runs.

Taste.description: Every knob of one scope, fully resolved.

hard_model.description: Where hard work goes. None is the top rung of the ladder.

parallel.description: Workers at once in a project, 1 to 100. `delegate_task` refuses one more.

tier.description: The costliest model tier a worker may run on.

default_effort.description: The effort a worker gets when the call names none. None leaves it to the model.

max_effort.description: The most effort a call may ask for.

budget_cents.description: What one worker may spend, in US cents, as its transcript prices it. 0 sets no cap.

time_limit_min.description: Minutes a worker runs before pinned stops it: the default and the ceiling of `limitMs`.

box_budget_cents.description: A box's budget in US cents: the default and the ceiling of its `budget_usd`. 0 sets neither.

box_size.description:
The size of a box opened with none named: the Captains' is the account's default, a
project's overrides it. None is the built-in default, small. The orchestrator's is never
set, since every box belongs to a project. Always written, null included, so a page tells a
hub that has it from one that predates it.

TaskRecord.description: One finished delegated task, as the hub keeps it for the account.

machine.description: The machine whose registry holds the task. The hub stamps both from the socket.

tier.description: The model's cost tier: low, mid or high.

limit.description: The limit that stopped it: `time`, or `budget` once spend is enforced.

asked_account.description: The account the request asked for, when a usage limit moved the task to `account`.

asked_model.description: The model the request asked for, when a usage limit moved the task to `model`.

moved_because.description: Why the task ran elsewhere than asked: the limit that stopped the account it asked for.

thread.description: The worker thread that showed it, on `machine`.

RunTarget.description: Where the task ran, from its delegator's side.

oneOf.description: On another machine of the account than its delegator's, which `machine` names.
pinned stopped it at one of its limits, which `limit` names.

Review.description:

oneOf.description: A commit message for `files`, or every change, written by a headless claude.
Commits `files`, or every change, with `message`.
Pushes the branch, setting its upstream on `origin` the first time.
Opens a pull request of the branch with gh, titled and described from its commits.
Fast-forwards the branch to its upstream.
Makes the folder a git repository.
Creates `name` on GitHub with gh, as `origin`, and pushes to it.

runOnWorktreeCreate.description: Runs in a new worktree as it is made for a thread.

async.description: With `run_on_worktree_create`, claude starts only once the script exits.

runOnSettle.description: Runs in a thread's worktree when the thread settles.

side.description: `RIGHT` for the new side, `LEFT` for a removed line.

PrChange.description: A change to who is on a pull request, what is on it, and its review threads.

oneOf.description: Adds or takes back the viewer's `content` on `subject`, a comment, review or the pull request.
Asks `login`, a person or a team's `org/slug`, for a review, or takes the request back.
Resolves the review thread `thread`, or opens it again.
Rewrites the comment `id`, a remark on the pull request or, with `review`, on a line.

Reaction.description: GitHub's reactions, by the name its GraphQL API gives them.

oneOf.description: Merges the pull request and the unmerged layers under it, as GitHub's merge-async does.
Rebases every unmerged layer, bottom to top, onto the stack's base.

StackHead.description: A layer's head as the reader last saw it, so a stack that moved since is not acted on.

HubCall.description:
Account-level calls, answered by the hub. Names and arguments match the app's Tauri
commands, so the settings page sends either. The last three come only from machines,
forwarding a connector session's callbacks to the hub, which holds the keys.

`{"cmd":"connect_linear","key":"lin_api_…"}`, `{"cmd":"stage","connector":"c1","issue":"uuid","stage":"coding"}`

`linear::Account`.
`connectors::Suggestions`.

bot.description: The bot to remove; empty for the default bot, which is what an app before several bots means.

oneOf.description: `github::Account`.
`Vec<github::Repo>`, most recently pushed first.
`vercel::Account`, once the gateway took the key.
`Vec<vercel::Model>`: chat models tagged `structured-output`, and every decision model. The list needs no key.

Deletes the account's boxes before it forgets the keys.
`connectors::BoxAccess`.
`connectors::RepoInsight`: whether the global orchestrator may read the account's repos.
Allows or refuses the pending box question `id`.

The folder of `repo` on `machine`, cloned there with the account's GitHub token when it has
none, or into `dest` when given.
`Vec<sync::Project>`: the account's projects, most recently shared first.
From a machine: a project it syncs, which other machines then offer to clone.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::Entry>`, every file the hub holds for the project.
From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps the files.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::File>`.
From a machine: `null`. Sets the executable bit when the hub still stores each sha. Sends no bytes.
The connector as stored.

`Vec<schedule::Task>`: the account's scheduled tasks, soonest first, each with its next run
and its last run.

`schedule::SaveAnswer`. A task with no id is new; the hub gives it one. The hub validates it,
computes `next_at`, and keeps who created it. With `dry_run` it only answers the next three run
times in the task's zone, and stores nothing.
The task as stored: paused (`enabled` false) or running again.
`Vec<schedule::TaskRun>`: the task's runs, newest first. No `limit` answers 20.

The account's release-protection switch: tag and main protection exist, so a task may be
pre-approved for a release. Only the user's app sets it; no agent action does. Answers `on`.

`RunStarted`: a session of the saved workflow `id`, started now with no trigger behind it,
on the machine the workflow names and under the limits of its project there.
Kept for older apps, whose Generate with AI button still sends it. The hub answers an error: an agent creates a workflow with `save_connector`.
Starts an interactive session on a new Upstash Box cloning `repo`. Returns `BoxStatus`.

size.description: None follows the project's and the account's default box size (`Tastes::box_size`).

oneOf.description: `BoxStatus` for the box behind `machine`, or an error when it is no box.
Adds `extra_usd` to the box behind `machine`'s budget. Returns `BoxStatus`.
`Vec<MachineView>`.

From a machine: `Vec<MachineView>`, each online machine with the summary it last reported, for
`orchestrator_capabilities`.

From a machine: `placement::Placed`, the machine of the account that runs a heavy worker it
would start, by the account's placement policy. `repo` is the project's origin, `need` the
account and model the worker runs on, and `exclude` the machines that refused it already.
`PairCode`.
`NewInvite`: a single-use code that lets one person create their own account on this hub.
`Invites`: the hub's signup mode and the account's codes nobody has used yet.

A signed-out app's connectors, moved to the account on its first sign-in.

slack_keys.description: Each Slack bot's token by bot id. `slack_key` stays the default bot's.

oneOf.description:
What a connector's session works on, which its callbacks into pinned report against.
Untagged, so a stage message from a Linear session reads `"issue": "<id>"` as it always has.

anyOf.title: LinearIssue
anyOf.description: Linear's id for the issue, which `pinned stage` moves.

anyOf.title: SlackThread
anyOf.description: The Slack thread `pinned slack reply` answers in, and whose filed issue `pinned stage` moves.

oneOf.description: From a workflow session's `pinned run set`: stores `value` as `{{vars.<name>}}` of its live graph run.

anyOf.title: LinearIssue
