anyOf.title: SlackThread
anyOf.description: The Slack thread `pinned slack reply` answers in, and whose filed issue `pinned stage` moves.

oneOf.description: `ExternalAgents`: the hub's MCP endpoint and the external agents the account let in.
`AgentRequest`: what the pending OAuth authorization `request` asks for, while it waits for the user.

`AgentRedirect`: lets the agent of the pending `request` in with `scopes` on `projects`, and
answers where the browser goes next, the agent's redirect with a one-use code.
`AgentRedirect`: refuses the pending `request`, and answers the agent's redirect with `access_denied`.
`null`. Ends the agent's access at once: its tokens stop working.

From a machine: `global_orchestrator::Handoff` of the machine `to` names. Carries a message
from the global orchestrator to a Capitão on another machine, or a Capitão's report up to the
account's global orchestrator. `request_id` makes a repeat answer the first outcome.

`global_orchestrator::Overview`: the account's projects on every machine, and what waits on
the user.

From a machine: the latest replies of the Capitão of the project at `path` on `machine`, as
`reading::read` answers them, with `project` set to `path`.

`taste::Tastes`: the account's, or the defaults while it has none. A machine asks too, when it
starts a Capitão or the global orchestrator.
`taste::Tastes`, once `patch` is applied to `scope` as `Tastes::set` does.
`taste::Tastes`, once `field` of `scope` is back to what it inherits.
From a machine: `true` when the account had no tastes and took these, a signed-out app's own.

`taste::BoxSizeChoice`: the size a box cloning `repo` opens at when its call names `size`,
or none, and which setting chose it. Without `repo`, a box of no project: the account's.

`taste::Tastes`, once the default box size of `repo`'s project, or the account's without
`repo`, is `size`. No `size` clears it: the project inherits the account's again, and the
account's goes back to the built-in small.

From the machine that hosts the global orchestrator, for its tab `tab`: `Call::RepoLook` of
`project` (a key `projects` lists) on `machine`, an id or a name, else on the checkout a
Capitão runs in, the asking machine's own, or the first online one; with `machine`,
`machine_name` and `project` set. Refused while the account's `RepoInsight` is off, and past
30 calls a minute or 300 an hour. Each call writes an audit row.

From a machine: `Call::ReadSession` of the tab `tab` on `machine`, an id or a name, else on
the online machine that has that tab, with `id`, `machine` and `machine_name` set.

From a machine: the started task's JSON. Runs `request` on the machine or in the Upstash Box
its target names, for the asking machine's tab `tab`, whose own id for the task is `task`.
`repo` is the caller's git origin, which the worker's checkout is found or cloned by;
`access` is the widest the caller may hand a child; `delegator` and `limits` are who asked
and the limits it runs under, which the worker is held to and recorded with.

From a machine: the status JSON of the task its tab `tab` delegated to `machine` as `task`,
or its state once cancelled when `cancel` gives a reason.

From a machine: `null` once machine `to` took the end of the task its tab `tab` delegated
here as `task`.

From a machine: `true` once machine `to` took what the worker of the task its tab `tab`
delegated here as `task` waits on the user for. No `ask` says it waits on nothing now.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`. Keeps `token`, a `claude setup-token` token, for
boxes that run as the pinned account `name`, which `delegate_task`'s `providerInstanceId` picks.
`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, without the token kept for `name`.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, once `machine` ran `claude setup-token` for its
Claude account `account` and the hub kept the token it printed under that name. The token
reaches no client.
Whether `machine` was still waiting on a `MintBoxClaudeToken` for `account`, which this stops.

From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps these records of its delegated tasks, as they
are now. The hub stamps the machine, and box time for a machine that is a box.

`delegate::DelegationStats` of the account's delegated tasks that ended in the last `days`
(1, 7 or 30), on every machine.

`Vec<delegate::UnclaimedEnd>`: the account's worker ends that the machine whose tab delegated
the task answered it did not take, as a machine that restarted and forgot the task does.
The hub keeps each for 30 days, newest first.

`upstash::BoxUsage`: the account's Upstash Box usage, and pinned's count of the box time its
delegated tasks used this UTC month. The Upstash key stays on the hub.

`Vec<upstash::StuckBox>`: the account's boxes pinned could not delete, with why, from the
hub's own record and rows. It reads no Upstash key and calls no Upstash.
`Vec<marks::SessionMarks>`: how the user filed each of the account's conversations.

`Vec<marks::SessionMarks>` of the sessions `changes` named, as they are once each change
landed in order. One left with only its id has no mark. The account's clients hear the same
as `ToClient::SessionMarks`.

`marks::SessionMarks` of the conversation in `tab` on `machine`, once it is archived: its tab
closed, and Settings › Archive lists it to bring back with its name and pin. Refused while
its turn runs.

`marks::SessionMarks` of the conversation in `tab`, once it is archived as `ArchiveSession`
does it. Only the machine that runs the tab sends it, from its auto-archive check, and the
hub keeps a pinned thread, an orchestrator and a working one open.

`Target`: the new tab, on the archived conversation's machine, that resumes it with its name
and pin back.

`null`, once the conversation's tab closed and its marks are gone, so pinned forgets it.
Claude Code keeps its transcript.

From a machine: `surface::ActAnswer` of an agent session's `act`, run as the account under
`surface::ACTIONS`, audited, and for a `confirm` action held for the user's approval.

`Vec<surface::Confirmation>`: the account's confirmations waiting on the user, oldest first,
then the last 20 decided, newest first.

From a signed-in client: `surface::Decided`. Approving runs the action for the session that
asked; either way the session gets a notice. `entered` holds what the user typed in the app
for a credential action's asked fields (`surface::Action::asks`); a credential action whose
run fails waits again, so the user can type another.

From a signed-in client: `surface::Unlocked`, once `password` is the account's. Until its
`until`, this connection runs the calls only the owner makes.

`Vec<surface::AuditEntry>`: the account's audit trail of agents' acts, newest first, `limit`
rows (50, at most 200) from unix second `before` and earlier, so a page repeats the rows of
its boundary second, which the client drops by id.

`Vec<mcp::Entry>`: the account's own MCP servers, which every session pinned starts loads
while enabled, each with the names of its secrets and never their values.

`Vec<ideas::Idea>`: the account's ideas, the most recently changed first; with `project` (a repo key),
only that project's.

`ideas::Idea`: adds an idea, or with `id` changes that one (its title, text and project as sent, and its
status when sent). The hub sets who made it and the times.
Removes the account's idea `id`.

`mcp::Entry`: adds a server, enabled, or with `id` changes that one, keeping its enabled
state. `secrets` holds what the user typed in the app; a name left out or blank keeps the
value the server has, and a new name needs one.
`mcp::Entry`: turns a server of the account's list on or off for the sessions started next.
Removes a server and its secrets from the account's list.

`mcp::Entry`: adds the server `name` that the Claude Code account `account` on `machine`
configures (`Call::McpImportable`), for every project or for `project` (a repository),
with `secrets` typed in the app for each of its names.

From a machine only: `Vec<mcp::Load>`, the account's enabled servers with their secrets, to
load into the sessions it starts.

`convex::Connection`, once Convex took the deploy key: connects its deployment to `repos`
(repo keys, as `github.com/owner/repo`) beside the ones it had. A repo moves off any other
deployment. Only the hub keeps Convex keys, so this has no Tauri command.

`convex::Connection`: sets the repos whose sessions read the deployment `id`, moving each
off any other deployment.
Forgets the deployment `id` and its key. Succeeds when it is already gone.
The table names of the deployment `id`, sorted, for the Read Convex data step.

From a machine only: what a Convex tool of the session in `tab` asks, in the project whose
repo key is `repo`. A read answers its text; `offer` answers what the session may read.

BoxAccess.description: The account's choice for each kind of actor.

oneOf.description: A new box for each issue or thread.
One box for this kind of actor.
Open nothing until the user says yes on the Upstash card. A Slack thread also gets one post.

RepoInsight.description:
Whether the global orchestrator may read the account's repositories with its repo tools. Off
until the user turns it on in Settings.

Project.description: A project of the account, offered on machines that don't have it yet.

repo.description: The origin as the machine that shared it has it, which clones it elsewhere.

File.description: A file as the hub holds it. An empty `sha` marks a deleted one.

modified.description: Unix milliseconds the file last changed on the machine that sent it.

size.description: Compressed bytes.

executable.description: Unix mode when the sender read one. Absent when the sender does not know the mode.

data.description: The contents gzipped, in base64; none for a deleted file.

ModeRepair.description:
Sets the executable bit on a file the hub already stores, without sending bytes.
The hub applies it only while that file's sha is still `sha`.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; empty keeps claude's default.

worktree.description: Runs each session in its own git worktree, so parallel issues don't share a checkout.

since.description:
Only issues created after this instant (RFC 3339) trigger, so saving a connector
doesn't start sessions for the backlog. Slack connectors move it forward on every check.

handled.description: Issues, or Slack threads as `<channel id>:<thread ts>`, that already started a session.

team.description: The Linear team a Slack connector's sessions file issues in, by name or key.

label.description: The Linear label put on the issues a Slack connector's sessions file; empty puts none.

fix.description: Whether a Slack connector's sessions may file a Linear issue and fix the bug.

created.description: The issue each Slack thread's session filed, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

followed.description: How far each handled Slack thread was passed on to its session, by `<channel id>:<thread ts>`.

proof.description: Whether a session that opens a pull request must prove it works, with a Playwright video.

ask.description: Asks a gateway model about the trigger's find before the session starts. None skips it.

account.description: The account its sessions run under; empty runs them under their project's.

slackBot.description:
The id of the Slack bot that watches and answers for it; empty is the default bot. A called
workflow answers with the bot of the thread it was handed instead.

graph.description:
The workflow drawn as a graph. None runs the fixed pipeline the fields above describe.
Older apps neither send nor read it.

oneOf.description: A Linear issue created with this label.
A Slack message in this channel, by name or id, that mentions the bot.

Every new message people start in this channel, by name or id, which a decision model sorts
into one of `decide`'s categories. The workflow has no session of its own.

A Slack thread a message workflow's category hands it, which its session answers as a
mention's session would. It watches no channel of its own.

Decide.description: How a message workflow sorts each message, and where each category sends it.

model.description: A decision model on the Vercel AI Gateway, such as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

fallback.description: The category, by name, that takes a message the model is unsure about. None keeps its guess.

description.description: What the decision model reads to tell this category from the others.

workflow.description:
The id of the `slack-mention` or `called` workflow that then owns the thread. None stops
at the category.

mention.description: A Slack user group, by handle or id, paged in the thread of each message in the category.

Columns.description: The Linear column each stage moves the issue to. Empty leaves the issue where it is.

Fix.description: How far a Slack connector's session goes with a bug it finds.

oneOf.description: Analyze and reply; never file an issue or change code.
Analyze, then ask in the thread; file and fix only once someone answered it with a mention.
Fix obvious bugs right away, and ask about the rest.

Filed.description: A Linear issue a Slack thread's session filed.

cursor.description: The newest message the session has seen, as a Slack ts.

seen.description: The newest message pinned read, when people wrote past `cursor` without mentioning the bot.

replied.description: Someone mentioned the bot in the thread after its session started, which `Fix::Ask` waits for.

Ask.description: A model on Vercel's AI Gateway that reads what the trigger found before the session starts.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`. The id picks chat or decision when the step runs.

name.description: The key the answer goes under, as `kind`.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text.

stopOn.description: Choices that end the workflow without a session.

RunsOn.description:
Where a workflow's sessions run. Kept under the connector's original `machine` key: a machine
id string ("" = any), or `{"kind":"upstash-box",…}`. Old stores load as before, and an old UI
that never touches the select saves the object back untouched.

size.description:
Left out when the workflow names none. A workflow saved before the default box size
always has one, since the old app wrote its default, medium, out.

edges.description: Order matters: a port's edges run in this order, each branch to its end before the next.

Node.description:
Everything a node can be. The session can also do most of these through `pinned` callbacks;
when both a node and the session post the same reply or file the same issue, the second write
is skipped, whichever runs first. Coding and review moves named in the connector's `columns`
stay implicit prompt instructions, alongside any `move-column` step.

Slack follow-ups in the thread are not a node. While the run's session is open, new thread
messages are typed into it, as today.

position.description: Canvas pixels of the node's center. The editor owns them.

group_name.description: The named group box the editor draws this node in. The runner ignores it.

oneOf.description: What starts a run. The walk begins at its outgoing edges.
One Vercel AI Gateway call that answers every question, and branches on one of them.
Branches on an answer an earlier classify already gave. No model call.

Tells the run's one Claude session something. The first `talk` of a run opens the session
with the session owner's settings; every later one, on any branch, types into it.

Opens the run's session with this step's own setup, then works like `talk`: the first
`session` of a run opens it, every later one types into it. Empty text fields inherit the
session owner's settings, so a bare node behaves exactly like `talk`.
Pings a Slack user group, by handle or id, in the run's thread.
Moves the Linear issue to the connector's `picked` column, as opening a session does today.

Posts `text` in the run's Slack thread, hub-side. A second post of the same text in the
same run is skipped, whether the node or the session posts first.

Files a Linear issue for the run's Slack thread, hub-side, linking back to the thread.
An issue the thread already filed is answered, never filed twice.

Works the run's Slack thread on an existing issue: the named identifier, or the issue
the thread already filed when empty.
Moves the run's Linear issue to the named column.

Requires a proof video on the pull request: like the connector's proof flag, it appends
the proof instructions to the session's opening prompt. The session still records the video.

Lets the run's session read the Convex deployment `connection` names: every table, or only
`tables`, which also turns off queries and logs. Like `proof`, it counts anywhere in the
workflow's own graph, and it adds a note to the session's opening prompt.
Walks another connector's graph inside this run, with this run's session.
Ends this branch on purpose. A port with no edge also ends its branch.

Watch.description: The trigger kinds, without the routing a fixed-pipeline `SlackMessage` carried in `Decide`.

oneOf.description: Runs only when another graph `call`s it.

name.description: The key the answer goes under in the run's context.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text and cannot be branched on.

description.description: What the model reads to tell this choice from the others.

PortId.description: A choice's stable id, or one of the fixed ports below. Reordering or renaming choices keeps edges.

oneOf.description: The port is the model's choice.

Today's `Decide::pick`: below `unsure_below` the fallback takes it, and below `page_at` a
choice whose branch pages a group gives way to the likeliest quiet one, or to `nowhere`.
An unsure answer keeps the model's guess.
An unsure answer takes this existing choice's port, as a `Decide` fallback category does.
An unsure answer takes an extra `fallback` port.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

branchOn.description: The name of the question whose choices are the ports. None leaves one `out` port.

Switch.description: Reads one answer from `classify` and takes the first case that matches, ignoring ASCII case.

cases.description: In order. The first `equals` that matches the answer wins.

SessionSetup.description:
The session setup a `session` step carries. Empty text fields inherit the session owner's
own session settings; `worktree` set here opens a separate worktree even when the owner would
share the checkout.

prompt.description: What this step tells the session, appended to the owner's opening prompt on open.

folder.description: The folder the session opens in; empty inherits the owner's.

repo.description: The repository a machine without the folder clones; empty inherits the owner's.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; empty keeps the owner's model.

effort.description: low, medium, high, xhigh or max; empty inherits the owner's effort.

permission.description: manual, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions or plan; empty inherits.

account.description: The account id its session runs under; empty runs the project's account.

worktree.description: Whether the session gets its own git worktree.

instructions.description: Instructions sent before the subject; empty inherits the owner's.

tz.description: IANA name, as `America/Sao_Paulo`; set from the creator's device.

grace_mins.description: Minutes after `due_at` during which a run still counts as on time. None = [`DEFAULT_GRACE_MINS`].

on_missed.description: What to do with a run that was not delivered within grace. None = `OnMissed::default_for(schedule)`.

pickup_mins.description: Minutes a delivered run may wait for its target to start it. None = [`DEFAULT_PICKUP_MINS`].

fyi.description:
Hub-computed, read-only: when an agent created the task and the user has not looked yet. The
Inbox shows a row for it. Unix seconds.

oneOf.description: A wall-clock date and time in the task's zone: `2026-11-13T09:00`.
Five-field cron, evaluated in the task's zone.
The user: a notification on every device, with no agent run.
The global Orchestrator, on the machine that hosts it.
A project's Captain, by repo key; an empty machine means wherever `send_to_captain` would pick.
An existing conversation, by Claude session id, so it survives tab restarts.
A new worker in a project, placed like `delegate_task`.
Text the target receives as one prompt.
Run now of a saved workflow. The target is ignored: the workflow's own `runs_on` decides.
The run becomes `missed` and the user decides: Run now or Skip.
Record the run as `skipped`; the next occurrence comes as usual.
Run as soon as a path opens, whenever that is.

Approval.description: A step the task may take without asking: that item, in that repo, when the command contains the text.

NeverItem.description: The items of the never list, in the order of the design's table.

Fallback2.description: Where a run goes when its target's machine is not there.

oneOf.description: Wait within the grace window. A box costs money, so this is the default.
Open a box, for the targets that allow it.

Actor.description: Who created a task or an idea: the user, or an agent by the part it plays.

ActorRole.description: The part the session that acted plays, as its tab shows it.

Need.description: What a worker needs from the machine that runs it.

Stage.description: Where a connector's session is in its work on an issue. Each stage maps to a Linear column.

oneOf.description: The harness picked the issue up and opened a session for it.
The session is about to change code.
The session opened the pull request.

AgentProject.description: A project an external agent may work in: one folder on one machine.

RelayTo.description: Where a relayed message goes, and what it carries.

oneOf.description:
`text` for the Capitão of the project at `path` on `machine`, as `Call::Enqueue` takes it.
The hub takes it only from the machine that hosts the account's global orchestrator.

A report for the account's global orchestrator, as `Call::OrchestratorReport` takes it. The
hub takes it only from a machine whose Capitão tab `report.tab` works in `report.path`.

`text` for the Capitão of `repo` in an Upstash Box the hub opens with the account's own
connection, or the box that already runs it. Taken only from the global orchestrator's host.

size.description: None follows the project's and the account's default box size.

TastePatch.description: A scope's own changes; a field left out inherits. A patch can set `hard_model` but not clear it.

box_size.description:
A project's box size over the account's. A patch can set it but not clear it; resetting
the field clears it.

placement.description:
The account's placement policy. Only the Captains' and the orchestrator's scope take it:
it belongs to the account, and a project's own comes later.

Strategy.description: How a worker climbs the model ladder.

oneOf.description: The cheapest rung with a detailed brief, re-briefed narrower before it moves up.
The cheapest rung, one rung up after two failures.
The hard model from the start.

ModelRef.description: A model as `orchestrator_capabilities` names it, and the provider it runs through when that matters.

Autonomy.description: What the agents decide without the user.

Placement.description: An account's placement policy, in Settings › Way of working.

avoid.description:
Machine ids never chosen by rank. One runs a worker only as the machine that asked, when
nothing else fits.

oneOf.description:
Workers with `isolation: "worktree"`. A shared worker works in the caller's checkout, and
another machine would not see its uncommitted changes.

TasteField.description: One knob of a `Taste`, named as its JSON field.

projects.description: Each project's changes over `captains`, by repo.

placement.description: Where the account's heavy delegated work runs.

Taste.description: Every knob of one scope, fully resolved.

hard_model.description: Where hard work goes. None is the top rung of the ladder.

parallel.description: Workers at once in a project, 1 to 100. `delegate_task` refuses one more.

tier.description: The costliest model tier a worker may run on.

default_effort.description: The effort a worker gets when the call names none. None leaves it to the model.

max_effort.description: The most effort a call may ask for.

budget_cents.description: What one worker may spend, in US cents, as its transcript prices it. 0 sets no cap.

time_limit_min.description: Minutes a worker runs before pinned stops it: the default and the ceiling of `limitMs`.

box_budget_cents.description: A box's budget in US cents: the default and the ceiling of its `budget_usd`. 0 sets neither.

box_size.description:
The size of a box opened with none named: the Captains' is the account's default, a
project's overrides it. None is the built-in default, small. The orchestrator's is never
set, since every box belongs to a project. Always written, null included, so a page tells a
hub that has it from one that predates it.

TaskRecord.description: One finished delegated task, as the hub keeps it for the account.

machine.description: The machine whose registry holds the task. The hub stamps both from the socket.

tier.description: The model's cost tier: low, mid or high.

limit.description: The limit that stopped it: `time`, or `budget` once spend is enforced.

asked_account.description: The account the request asked for, when a usage limit moved the task to `account`.

asked_model.description: The model the request asked for, when a usage limit moved the task to `model`.

moved_because.description: Why the task ran elsewhere than asked: the limit that stopped the account it asked for.

thread.description: The worker thread that showed it, on `machine`.

RunTarget.description: Where the task ran, from its delegator's side.

oneOf.description: On another machine of the account than its delegator's, which `machine` names.
pinned stopped it at one of its limits, which `limit` names.

Review.description:
Whether the delegator used the result. `auto` marks one pinned set from a signal: the
task's pull request merged, or the same delegator started a task with the same title again.

Mark.description: One change to one mark. `{"title":"Fix login"}`, `{"pin":null}`, `"clear"`.

oneOf.description: Drops every mark of the session.

until.description: Unix seconds it comes back to the inbox.

limit.description: The usage limit's `resume_at` this snooze waits out, when it snoozed a limited thread.

Archived.description: What Unarchive needs to start the conversation again, and what the Archive page shows.

machine.description: The machine whose tab it was, which resumes it.

cwd.description: The tab's folder, where the session resumes.

name.description: The thread's title when it was archived.

created.description: Unix seconds of its first message.

title.description: The name the user had given it, back on the thread when it is unarchived.

pinned.description: It was pinned, and is pinned again when it is unarchived.

AgentAct.description:
An agent session's `act`, as its machine passes it to the hub. The hub reads the session's role
and Claude session from the tabs that machine reported, never from here.

args.description: The action's fields, as `actions` describes them.

request_id.description: Makes a repeat answer the first outcome instead of running again.

machine.description: The machine a `Call` runs on, an id or a name; the session's own when absent.

Spec.description: A server of the account's list, as the app and agents write it.

name.description: What sessions call it, and what its tools are named after: letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

project.description:
The one project it loads in, as its repository (`github.com/owner/repo`); every project
when absent.

Reach.description:
How pinned starts or reaches a server of the account's list, as Claude Code's own config
names it. Environment and header values are secrets, so only their names are here.

oneOf.description: A program pinned starts beside the session.

env.description: The environment variables it gets. The user types each value in the app.

oneOf.description: A streamable HTTP endpoint.

headers.description: The headers sent with each request. The user types each value in the app.

oneOf.description: A server-sent events endpoint.

Secrets.description: The secret values of a server, by name: never in an answer, a list, an audit row or an error.

ConvexAsk.description: What a session asks. Tool `convex_<op>` sends `{"op":"<op>",…}`. `Offer` has no tool.

oneOf.description: What this tab may read, asked by `pinned mcp` at tools/list.
With no table: the table names. With a table: its fields and indexes.
The body of `async (ctx) => { … }`, run as a read-only query.
A deployed query by path, `invoices:byNumber`.

raw.description: The final phrases exactly as the recognizer returned them, one per line.

cleaned.description: The same phrases after the composer's cleanup, one per line.

final_text.description: The composer's text when the session ended.

session the user rated and agreed to share. Text only, never audio.

raw.description: The final phrases exactly as the recognizer returned them, one per line.

cleaned.description: The same phrases after the composer's cleanup, one per line.

final_text.description: The composer's text when the session ended.

`{"type":"auth","token":"…","name":"mac-mini","os":"macos","version":"0.6.0"}`,
`{"type":"call","id":7,"call":{"cmd":"slack_reply","connector":"c2","channel":"C1","thread":"1.2","text":"done"}}`

oneOf.description: The answer to `ToMachine::Call` with this id.
A tab's output for the viewer that subscribed to it, its screen first.
A connector session's callback; the hub answers with `ToMachine::Reply`.

Reply.description: The answer to the call that carried `id`: `{"id":4,"ok":…}` or `{"id":4,"err":"…"}`.

MachineEvent.description:
What a machine reports on its own.

`{"kind":"exit","tab":"tab-1"}`, `{"kind":"output","tab":"tab-1","data":"aGk="}`

oneOf.description: Every tab, after any of them opened, closed, started, exited or changed status, title or folder.
Output of a tab a client attached to, as the hub passes it on.
The tab's claude exited by itself.
The account's usage, after its session reported it.
The transcript of a tab this client watches changed. The client reads it with `Call::Thread`.
Some while this process is installing a release, None when it connects with nothing in progress.
Skills in these scopes changed on disk, by a save or a sync pull. An open Skills page lists again.
A taste chat's session changed the account's tastes. An open Way of working page reads them again.

The machine's load and accounts, every 20 seconds. The hub keeps the latest as `MachineView::state`
and passes it to no client.

Whether the desktop app runs in the background, with no window: when it connects and after
each change. A machine without the app never sends it. The hub keeps it as
`MachineView::background` and passes the event to no client.

account.description: The account the tab's sessions run under.

message.description: What the session asks, while it needs input.

resume_at.description: Unix time a usage limit lifts, while one stopped the turn.

held.description: The session waits out its usage limit without continuing by itself when it lifts.

subject.description: What the connector's session works on.

opened.description: The tab's number, which orders tabs by when they opened.

updated.description: Unix time the session last reported a status.

session.description: Claude Code's id for the conversation, which outlives the tab's id across restarts.

interrupted.description: A turn was running when pinned quit, so the tab has work left to continue.

cut_by_sleep.description: The turn died on an API error while the machine slept, so it stopped where the sleep cut it.

stats.description: What the conversation's work came to so far, once its transcript holds any of it.

branch.description: The git branch of the conversation's last message.

pr.description: The last pull request the conversation opened or worked on.

last_message_at.description: Unix seconds of the conversation's last message.

prompt_title.description:
The conversation's first prompt, its first line cut short. It stands in for `title`, which
a restored tab has lost until its next prompt.

role.description: The tab is its project's orchestrator, or a worker the orchestrator started.

spawned_by.description:
The tab that started this one: the thread that delegated a worker, or the thread whose
delegated task this tab reopened. The sidebar nests the tab under it.

spawned_on.description:
The machine whose tab `spawned_by` names, when that tab is on another machine: a worker a
thread there delegated here.

orchestrator_global.description:
The tab is the account's global orchestrator, the chat above every project's Capitão. Its
`role` is empty, so an older app shows it as a plain thread.

orchestrator_turn.description:
The tab is a Capitão running a turn that a message from the global orchestrator started,
which it may not have reported yet: a message to it queues.

queued.description:
How many messages wait for the tab to go idle before they are typed into it: its workers'
news and the global orchestrator's requests.

work.description:
What the thread and the workers it delegated cost so far, on the thread that delegated
them. Workers are not counted again under it: its card is the one place the total shows.

taste_chat.description:
The tab was opened from the Way of working page to adjust the account's tastes by talking,
and its session has the taste tools. Its `role` is empty, so an older app shows a plain thread.

question.description:
What the session's last finished turn asked the user, read from its last reply. Cleared when
the next turn starts or fails.

ask_detail.description:
While the session waits on an approval or a question mid-turn: the tool call or the question
it waits on, read from its transcript, such as the command a permission prompt shows.

alive.description: A process runs the tab's session now. `running` also holds for a conversation that sleeps.

asleep.description: The conversation sleeps with no process: a message wakes it.

headless.description: The tab shows a headless child, which works with no session of the tab's own.

stopped.description: Why the tab's last process ended mid-turn, until a new turn or input starts it again.

questions.description:
The questionnaire the session waits on the user to answer, which `Call::AnswerQuestions`
answers. While it is open the tab reads as a question mid-turn, so an app that predates it
still shows the tab waiting.

read_only.description:
The session acts read-only whatever `bypass` says: its permission mode is plan, or a key
press left the mode unknown until a hook reports it. An older node never sends it.

oneOf.description: The account's agent CLI, a session that may be resumed.
The CLI's login for the account, never resumed.
The turn died on an API error, such as a usage limit.

Subject.description:
What a connector's session works on, which its callbacks into pinned report against.
Untagged, so a stage message from a Linear session reads `"issue": "<id>"` as it always has.

anyOf.title: LinearIssue
anyOf.description: Linear's id for the issue, which `pinned stage` moves.

anyOf.title: SlackThread
anyOf.description: The Slack thread `pinned slack reply` answers in, and whose filed issue `pinned stage` moves.

CutBySleep.description: When the machine slept: the last tick before it and the first after it, in unix seconds.

ThreadStats.description: What a thread's work came to, read from its transcript.

active_ms.description: How long the agent worked on the thread's turns, unknown when the entrypoint logs no turn durations.

cost_usd.description: Claude Code's own estimate at API prices, subagents included.

PrLink.description: A pull request a conversation opened or worked on.

Role.description: The part a session plays in its project's orchestration.

oneOf.description: Hands every request to workers.
Does one task another session delegated, and may delegate parts of it in turn.

WorkTotal.description: What a thread's card shows of its rollup: the cost of its own session and its workers, added up.

usd.description: The known costs, the thread's own session, agents and boxes together.

unknown.description: Parts whose cost is not known, which `usd` leaves out.

workers.description: Workers under the thread, theirs in turn included.

Questionnaire.description: The questions an agent asks the user in one go.

title.description: What the questions are about, in a few words.

projects.description: The project keys whose message from the global orchestrator waits on the answers.

header.description: A short chip label, such as `Branch`.

changes.description: What the agent does differently depending on the answer.

multi_select.description: The user may choose more than one option.

description.description: One line: what choosing it leads to.

tab.description: Id of the tab whose session fired the hook.

session.description: Claude Code's session id, which `claude --resume` takes.

title.description: A few words on what the session is about, once Claude Code named it or the user prompted.

resume_at.description: Unix time the usage limit that stopped the turn lifts, when the failure was one.

prompt.description: What the user asked, on the event that starts a turn.

snapshot.description: Git tree of the working tree, on the events that start and end a turn.

permission_mode.description: Claude Code's permission mode, such as `plan` or `default`. Absent when the hook does not report one.

Usage.description:
How much of the subscription's rate limits the account has used, as Claude Code's statusline
data reports it. Claude Code leaves out a window it has no figure for.

UpdateStatus.description: What a machine reports about replacing itself. `to` is the release it is moving to.

sessions.description: Sessions running now, of any role.

workers.description: Workers running now: worker sessions and delegated tasks.

workers_at_once.description: Workers at once that this machine allows a project, from the account's way of working.

reported_at.description: Unix seconds when the hub heard it. The hub sets it; a machine's own value is ignored.

Load.description: How busy a machine is. A field is None where the machine can't read it.

cpu_percent.description: The one-minute load average per core, as a percent capped at 100.

mem_available_mb.description: Memory that a new process can take without swapping: free, inactive and cached.

AccountState.description: One agent account of a machine, as far as a caller needs to choose it.

can_run_child_task.description: Signed in on that machine, with its CLI installed.

models.description: The model ids it offers a worker. Empty when it names none, as Codex does.

Account-level calls, answered by the hub. Names and arguments match the app's Tauri
commands, so the settings page sends either. The last three come only from machines,
forwarding a connector session's callbacks to the hub, which holds the keys.

`{"cmd":"connect_linear","key":"lin_api_…"}`, `{"cmd":"stage","connector":"c1","issue":"uuid","stage":"coding"}`

From a machine: `Vec<sync::File>`.

The connector as stored.

The task as stored: paused (`enabled` false) or running again.

Starts an interactive session on a new Upstash Box cloning `repo`. Returns `BoxStatus`.

Adds `extra_usd` to the box behind `machine`'s budget. Returns `BoxStatus`.
`Vec<MachineView>`.

`PairCode`.

oneOf.description: `ExternalAgents`: the hub's MCP endpoint and the external agents the account let in.
`AgentRequest`: what the pending OAuth authorization `request` asks for, while it waits for the user.

`AgentRedirect`: lets the agent of the pending `request` in with `scopes` on `projects`, and
answers where the browser goes next, the agent's redirect with a one-use code.
`AgentRedirect`: refuses the pending `request`, and answers the agent's redirect with `access_denied`.
`null`. Ends the agent's access at once: its tokens stop working.

From a machine: `global_orchestrator::Handoff` of the machine `to` names. Carries a message
from the global orchestrator to a Capitão on another machine, or a Capitão's report up to the
account's global orchestrator. `request_id` makes a repeat answer the first outcome.

`global_orchestrator::Overview`: the account's projects on every machine, and what waits on
the user.

From a machine: the latest replies of the Capitão of the project at `path` on `machine`, as
`reading::read` answers them, with `project` set to `path`.

`taste::Tastes`: the account's, or the defaults while it has none. A machine asks too, when it
starts a Capitão or the global orchestrator.
`taste::Tastes`, once `patch` is applied to `scope` as `Tastes::set` does.
`taste::Tastes`, once `field` of `scope` is back to what it inherits.
From a machine: `true` when the account had no tastes and took these, a signed-out app's own.

`taste::BoxSizeChoice`: the size a box cloning `repo` opens at when its call names `size`,
or none, and which setting chose it. Without `repo`, a box of no project: the account's.

`taste::Tastes`, once the default box size of `repo`'s project, or the account's without
`repo`, is `size`. No `size` clears it: the project inherits the account's again, and the
account's goes back to the built-in small.

From the machine that hosts the global orchestrator, for its tab `tab`: `Call::RepoLook` of
`project` (a key `projects` lists) on `machine`, an id or a name, else on the checkout a
Capitão runs in, the asking machine's own, or the first online one; with `machine`,
`machine_name` and `project` set. Refused while the account's `RepoInsight` is off, and past
30 calls a minute or 300 an hour. Each call writes an audit row.

From a machine: `Call::ReadSession` of the tab `tab` on `machine`, an id or a name, else on
the online machine that has that tab, with `id`, `machine` and `machine_name` set.

From a machine: the started task's JSON. Runs `request` on the machine or in the Upstash Box
its target names, for the asking machine's tab `tab`, whose own id for the task is `task`.
`repo` is the caller's git origin, which the worker's checkout is found or cloned by;
`access` is the widest the caller may hand a child; `delegator` and `limits` are who asked
and the limits it runs under, which the worker is held to and recorded with.

From a machine: the status JSON of the task its tab `tab` delegated to `machine` as `task`,
or its state once cancelled when `cancel` gives a reason.

From a machine: `null` once machine `to` took the end of the task its tab `tab` delegated
here as `task`.

From a machine: `true` once machine `to` took what the worker of the task its tab `tab`
delegated here as `task` waits on the user for. No `ask` says it waits on nothing now.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`. Keeps `token`, a `claude setup-token` token, for
boxes that run as the pinned account `name`, which `delegate_task`'s `providerInstanceId` picks.
`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, without the token kept for `name`.

`connectors::Settings::box_claude_tokens`, once `machine` ran `claude setup-token` for its
Claude account `account` and the hub kept the token it printed under that name. The token
reaches no client.
Whether `machine` was still waiting on a `MintBoxClaudeToken` for `account`, which this stops.

From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps these records of its delegated tasks, as they
are now. The hub stamps the machine, and box time for a machine that is a box.

`delegate::DelegationStats` of the account's delegated tasks that ended in the last `days`
(1, 7 or 30), on every machine.

`Vec<delegate::UnclaimedEnd>`: the account's worker ends that the machine whose tab delegated
the task answered it did not take, as a machine that restarted and forgot the task does.
The hub keeps each for 30 days, newest first.

`upstash::BoxUsage`: the account's Upstash Box usage, and pinned's count of the box time its
delegated tasks used this UTC month. The Upstash key stays on the hub.

`Vec<upstash::StuckBox>`: the account's boxes pinned could not delete, with why, from the
hub's own record and rows. It reads no Upstash key and calls no Upstash.
`Vec<marks::SessionMarks>`: how the user filed each of the account's conversations.

`Vec<marks::SessionMarks>` of the sessions `changes` named, as they are once each change
landed in order. One left with only its id has no mark. The account's clients hear the same
as `ToClient::SessionMarks`.

`marks::SessionMarks` of the conversation in `tab` on `machine`, once it is archived: its tab
closed, and Settings › Archive lists it to bring back with its name and pin. Refused while
its turn runs.

`marks::SessionMarks` of the conversation in `tab`, once it is archived as `ArchiveSession`
does it. Only the machine that runs the tab sends it, from its auto-archive check, and the
hub keeps a pinned thread, an orchestrator and a working one open.

`Target`: the new tab, on the archived conversation's machine, that resumes it with its name
and pin back.

`null`, once the conversation's tab closed and its marks are gone, so pinned forgets it.
Claude Code keeps its transcript.

From a machine: `surface::ActAnswer` of an agent session's `act`, run as the account under
`surface::ACTIONS`, audited, and for a `confirm` action held for the user's approval.

`Vec<surface::Confirmation>`: the account's confirmations waiting on the user, oldest first,
then the last 20 decided, newest first.

From a signed-in client: `surface::Decided`. Approving runs the action for the session that
asked; either way the session gets a notice. `entered` holds what the user typed in the app
for a credential action's asked fields (`surface::Action::asks`); a credential action whose
run fails waits again, so the user can type another.

From a signed-in client: `surface::Unlocked`, once `password` is the account's. Until its
`until`, this connection runs the calls only the owner makes.

`Vec<surface::AuditEntry>`: the account's audit trail of agents' acts, newest first, `limit`
rows (50, at most 200) from unix second `before` and earlier, so a page repeats the rows of
its boundary second, which the client drops by id.

`Vec<mcp::Entry>`: the account's own MCP servers, which every session pinned starts loads
while enabled, each with the names of its secrets and never their values.

`Vec<ideas::Idea>`: the account's ideas, the most recently changed first; with `project` (a repo key),
only that project's.

`ideas::Idea`: adds an idea, or with `id` changes that one (its title, text and project as sent, and its
status when sent). The hub sets who made it and the times.
Removes the account's idea `id`.

`mcp::Entry`: adds a server, enabled, or with `id` changes that one, keeping its enabled
state. `secrets` holds what the user typed in the app; a name left out or blank keeps the
value the server has, and a new name needs one.
`mcp::Entry`: turns a server of the account's list on or off for the sessions started next.
Removes a server and its secrets from the account's list.

`mcp::Entry`: adds the server `name` that the Claude Code account `account` on `machine`
configures (`Call::McpImportable`), for every project or for `project` (a repository),
with `secrets` typed in the app for each of its names.

From a machine only: `Vec<mcp::Load>`, the account's enabled servers with their secrets, to
load into the sessions it starts.

`convex::Connection`, once Convex took the deploy key: connects its deployment to `repos`
(repo keys, as `github.com/owner/repo`) beside the ones it had. A repo moves off any other
deployment. Only the hub keeps Convex keys, so this has no Tauri command.

`convex::Connection`: sets the repos whose sessions read the deployment `id`, moving each
off any other deployment.
Forgets the deployment `id` and its key. Succeeds when it is already gone.
The table names of the deployment `id`, sorted, for the Read Convex data step.

From a machine only: what a Convex tool of the session in `tab` asks, in the project whose
repo key is `repo`. A read answers its text; `offer` answers what the session may read.

RepoInsight.description:
Whether the global orchestrator may read the account's repositories with its repo tools. Off
until the user turns it on in Settings.

Project.description: A project of the account, offered on machines that don't have it yet.

repo.description: The origin as the machine that shared it has it, which clones it elsewhere.

executable.description: Unix mode when the sender read one. Absent when the sender does not know the mode.

worktree.description: Runs each session in its own git worktree, so parallel issues don't share a checkout.

since.description:

doesn't start sessions for the backlog. Slack connectors move it forward on every check.

handled.description: Issues, or Slack threads as `<channel id>:<thread ts>`, that already started a session.

team.description: The Linear team a Slack connector's sessions file issues in, by name or key.

label.description: The Linear label put on the issues a Slack connector's sessions file; empty puts none.

fix.description: Whether a Slack connector's sessions may file a Linear issue and fix the bug.

proof.description: Whether a session that opens a pull request must prove it works, with a Playwright video.

slackBot.description:

workflow answers with the bot of the thread it was handed instead.

graph.description:

Older apps neither send nor read it.

model.description: A decision model on the Vercel AI Gateway, such as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

fallback.description: The category, by name, that takes a message the model is unsure about. None keeps its guess.

workflow.description:

at the category.

mention.description: A Slack user group, by handle or id, paged in the thread of each message in the category.

Columns.description: The Linear column each stage moves the issue to. Empty leaves the issue where it is.

Fix.description: How far a Slack connector's session goes with a bug it finds.

oneOf.description: Analyze and reply; never file an issue or change code.

Fix obvious bugs right away, and ask about the rest.

Filed.description: A Linear issue a Slack thread's session filed.

cursor.description: The newest message the session has seen, as a Slack ts.

seen.description: The newest message pinned read, when people wrote past `cursor` without mentioning the bot.

replied.description: Someone mentioned the bot in the thread after its session started, which `Fix::Ask` waits for.

Ask.description: A model on Vercel's AI Gateway that reads what the trigger found before the session starts.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`. The id picks chat or decision when the step runs.

name.description: The key the answer goes under, as `kind`.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text.

stopOn.description: Choices that end the workflow without a session.

RunsOn.description:
Where a workflow's sessions run. Kept under the connector's original `machine` key: a machine
id string ("" = any), or `{"kind":"upstash-box",…}`. Old stores load as before, and an old UI
that never touches the select saves the object back untouched.

size.description:
Left out when the workflow names none. A workflow saved before the default box size
always has one, since the old app wrote its default, medium, out.

edges.description: Order matters: a port's edges run in this order, each branch to its end before the next.

Node.description:
Everything a node can be. The session can also do most of these through `pinned` callbacks;
when both a node and the session post the same reply or file the same issue, the second write
is skipped, whichever runs first. Coding and review moves named in the connector's `columns`
stay implicit prompt instructions, alongside any `move-column` step.

Slack follow-ups in the thread are not a node. While the run's session is open, new thread
messages are typed into it, as today.

position.description: Canvas pixels of the node's center. The editor owns them.

group_name.description: The named group box the editor draws this node in. The runner ignores it.

oneOf.description: What starts a run. The walk begins at its outgoing edges.
One Vercel AI Gateway call that answers every question, and branches on one of them.
Branches on an answer an earlier classify already gave. No model call.

Tells the run's one Claude session something. The first `talk` of a run opens the session
with the session owner's settings; every later one, on any branch, types into it.

`session` of a run opens it, every later one types into it. Empty text fields inherit the
session owner's settings, so a bare node behaves exactly like `talk`.
Pings a Slack user group, by handle or id, in the run's thread.
Moves the Linear issue to the connector's `picked` column, as opening a session does today.

Posts `text` in the run's Slack thread, hub-side. A second post of the same text in the
same run is skipped, whether the node or the session posts first.

Files a Linear issue for the run's Slack thread, hub-side, linking back to the thread.

Works the run's Slack thread on an existing issue: the named identifier, or the issue

workflow's own graph, and it adds a note to the session's opening prompt.
Walks another connector's graph inside this run, with this run's session.
Ends this branch on purpose. A port with no edge also ends its branch.

name.description: The key the answer goes under in the run's context.

choices.description: The answers the model must pick from; empty takes free text and cannot be branched on.

model.description: A gateway model id, as `typesafe-ai/jev`.

branchOn.description: The name of the question whose choices are the ports. None leaves one `out` port.

SessionSetup.description:

effort.description: low, medium, high, xhigh or max; empty inherits the owner's effort.

permission.description: manual, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions or plan; empty inherits.

account.description: The account id its session runs under; empty runs the project's account.

worktree.description: Whether the session gets its own git worktree.

instructions.description: Instructions sent before the subject; empty inherits the owner's.

tz.description: IANA name, as `America/Sao_Paulo`; set from the creator's device.

grace_mins.description: Minutes after `due_at` during which a run still counts as on time. None = [`DEFAULT_GRACE_MINS`].

on_missed.description: What to do with a run that was not delivered within grace. None = `OnMissed::default_for(schedule)`.

pickup_mins.description: Minutes a delivered run may wait for its target to start it. None = [`DEFAULT_PICKUP_MINS`].

fyi.description:

NeverItem.description: The items of the never list, in the order of the design's table.

Fallback2.description: Where a run goes when its target's machine is not there.

oneOf.description: Wait within the grace window. A box costs money, so this is the default.
Open a box, for the targets that allow it.

Actor.description: Who created a task or an idea: the user, or an agent by the part it plays.

ActorRole.description: The part the session that acted plays, as its tab shows it.

Need.description: What a worker needs from the machine that runs it.

Stage.description: Where a connector's session is in its work on an issue. Each stage maps to a Linear column.

oneOf.description: The harness picked the issue up and opened a session for it.
The session is about to change code.
The session opened the pull request.

AgentProject.description: A project an external agent may work in: one folder on one machine.

RelayTo.description: Where a relayed message goes, and what it carries.

oneOf.description:

What a Capitão tells the global orchestrator, at the end of a turn one of its messages started
or through `tell_orchestrator`.

project.description: The project's name, its folder's.

path.description: The project's folder on that machine.

answers.description:

One project's Capitão, by its repo as in `github.com/acme/site`.

A project's box size over the account's. A patch can set it but not clear it; resetting
the field clears it.

placement.description:
The account's placement policy. Only the Captains' and the orchestrator's scope take it:
it belongs to the account, and a project's own comes later.

The hard model from the start.

Autonomy.description: What the agents decide without the user.

oneOf.description: Haiku and flash models: sweeps, translations, first drafts.

Machine ids never chosen by rank. One runs a worker only as the machine that asked, when
nothing else fits.

Workers with `isolation: "worktree"`. A shared worker works in the caller's checkout, and
another machine would not see its uncommitted changes.

projects.description: Each project's changes over `captains`, by repo.

hard_model.description: Where hard work goes. None is the top rung of the ladder.

parallel.description: Workers at once in a project, 1 to 100. `delegate_task` refuses one more.

tier.description: The costliest model tier a worker may run on.

default_effort.description: The effort a worker gets when the call names none. None leaves it to the model.

max_effort.description: The most effort a call may ask for.

budget_cents.description: What one worker may spend, in US cents, as its transcript prices it. 0 sets no cap.

time_limit_min.description: Minutes a worker runs before pinned stops it: the default and the ceiling of `limitMs`.

project's overrides it. None is the built-in default, small. The orchestrator's is never

hub that has it from one that predates it.

start of the README, and the latest commits.

tracked paths that match it.

heavy.description: Whether the account's placement policy places this worker, over its rule for heavy work.

Access.description:

parent to read-only, and a parent that asks before acting does not hand the child a bypass.

an approval or a question. The machine that runs it reports it as it starts and again, as `None`,
once it is answered, and the thread that delegated the task keeps it until then.

tool.description: The tool an approval is for, such as `Bash`.

ask.description: What the thread asks, as its session said it.

since.description: Unix seconds the thread started to wait.

AskKind.description: What a session that cannot go on without the user asks of them.

machine.description: The machine whose registry holds the task. The hub stamps both from the socket.

tier.description: The model's cost tier: low, mid or high.

asked_model.description: The model the request asked for, when a usage limit moved the task to `model`.

moved_because.description: Why the task ran elsewhere than asked: the limit that stopped the account it asked for.

thread.description: The worker thread that showed it, on `machine`.

account.description: The account the tab's sessions run under.

message.description: What the session asks, while it needs input.

Subject.description:
What a connector's session works on, which its callbacks into pinned report against.
Untagged, so a stage message from a Linear session reads `"issue": "<id>"` as it always has.

anyOf.title: LinearIssue
anyOf.description: Linear's id for the issue, which `pinned stage` moves.

anyOf.title: SlackThread
anyOf.description: The Slack thread `pinned slack reply` answers in, and whose filed issue `pinned stage` moves.

CutBySleep.description: When the machine slept: the last tick before it and the first after it, in unix seconds.

ThreadStats.description: What a thread's work came to, read from its transcript.

active_ms.description: How long the agent worked on the thread's turns, unknown when the entrypoint logs no turn durations.

cost_usd.description: Claude Code's own estimate at API prices, subagents included.

PrLink.description: A pull request a conversation opened or worked on.

Role.description: The part a session plays in its project's orchestration.

oneOf.description: Hands every request to workers.
Does one task another session delegated, and may delegate parts of it in turn.

WorkTotal.description: What a thread's card shows of its rollup: the cost of its own session and its workers, added up.

usd.description: The known costs, the thread's own session, agents and boxes together.

unknown.description: Parts whose cost is not known, which `usd` leaves out.

workers.description: Workers under the thread, theirs in turn included.

Questionnaire.description: The questions an agent asks the user in one go.

title.description: What the questions are about, in a few words.

projects.description: The project keys whose message from the global orchestrator waits on the answers.

header.description: A short chip label, such as `Branch`.

changes.description: What the agent does differently depending on the answer.

multi_select.description: The user may choose more than one option.

description.description: One line: what choosing it leads to.

tab.description: Id of the tab whose session fired the hook.

session.description: Claude Code's session id, which `claude --resume` takes.

title.description: A few words on what the session is about, once Claude Code named it or the user prompted.

resume_at.description: Unix time the usage limit that stopped the turn lifts, when the failure was one.

prompt.description: What the user asked, on the event that starts a turn.

snapshot.description: Git tree of the working tree, on the events that start and end a turn.

permission_mode.description: Claude Code's permission mode, such as `plan` or `default`. Absent when the hook does not report one.

Usage.description:
How much of the subscription's rate limits the account has used, as Claude Code's statusline
data reports it. Claude Code leaves out a window it has no figure for.

UpdateStatus.description: What a machine reports about replacing itself. `to` is the release it is moving to.

sessions.description: Sessions running now, of any role.

workers.description: Workers running now: worker sessions and delegated tasks.

workers_at_once.description: Workers at once that this machine allows a project, from the account's way of working.

reported_at.description: Unix seconds when the hub heard it. The hub sets it; a machine's own value is ignored.

Load.description: How busy a machine is. A field is None where the machine can't read it.

cpu_percent.description: The one-minute load average per core, as a percent capped at 100.

mem_available_mb.description: Memory that a new process can take without swapping: free, inactive and cached.

AccountState.description: One agent account of a machine, as far as a caller needs to choose it.

can_run_child_task.description: Signed in on that machine, with its CLI installed.

models.description: The model ids it offers a worker. Empty when it names none, as Codex does.

HubCall.description:
Account-level calls, answered by the hub. Names and arguments match the app's Tauri
commands, so the settings page sends either. The last three come only from machines,
forwarding a connector session's callbacks to the hub, which holds the keys.

`{"cmd":"connect_linear","key":"lin_api_…"}`, `{"cmd":"stage","connector":"c1","issue":"uuid","stage":"coding"}`

oneOf.description: `connectors::Settings`.
`linear::Account`.
`connectors::Suggestions`.
`slack::Connected`: `slack::Account` with the bot and whether the token added it.

bot.description: The bot to remove; empty for the default bot, which is what an app before several bots means.

oneOf.description: Channel names.

bot.description: The bot whose channels to list; empty for the default bot.

oneOf.description: `github::Account`.
`Vec<github::Repo>`, most recently pushed first.
`vercel::Account`, once the gateway took the key.
`Vec<vercel::Model>`: chat models tagged `structured-output`, and every decision model. The list needs no key.
`upstash::Account`, once Upstash took the key. Only a signed-in app runs boxes, so this has no Tauri command.
Deletes the account's boxes before it forgets the keys.
`connectors::BoxAccess`.
`connectors::RepoInsight`: whether the global orchestrator may read the account's repos.
Allows or refuses the pending box question `id`.

The folder of `repo` on `machine`, cloned there with the account's GitHub token when it has
none, or into `dest` when given.
`Vec<sync::Project>`: the account's projects, most recently shared first.
From a machine: a project it syncs, which other machines then offer to clone.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::Entry>`, every file the hub holds for the project.
From a machine: `null`, once the hub keeps the files.
From a machine: `Vec<sync::File>`.
From a machine: `null`. Sets the executable bit when the hub still stores each sha. Sends no bytes.
The connector as stored.

`Vec<schedule::Task>`: the account's scheduled tasks, soonest first, each with its next run
and its last run.

`schedule::SaveAnswer`. A task with no id is new; the hub gives it one. The hub validates it,
computes `next_at`, and keeps who created it. With `dry_run` it only answers the next three run
times in the task's zone, and stores nothing.
The task as stored: paused (`enabled` false) or running again.
`Vec<schedule::TaskRun>`: the task's runs, newest first. No `limit` answers 20.

The account's release-protection switch: tag and main protection exist, so a task may be
pre-approved for a release. Only the user's app sets it; no agent action does. Answers `on`.

`RunStarted`: a session of the saved workflow `id`, started now with no trigger behind it,
on the machine the workflow names and under the limits of its project there.
Kept for older apps, whose Generate with AI button still sends it. The hub answers an error: an agent creates a workflow with `save_connector`.
Starts an interactive session on a new Upstash Box cloning `repo`. Returns `BoxStatus`.

size.description: None follows the project's and the account's default box size (`Tastes::box_size`).

oneOf.description: `BoxStatus` for the box behind `machine`, or an error when it is no box.
Adds `extra_usd` to the box behind `machine`'s budget. Returns `BoxStatus`.
`Vec<MachineView>`.

From a machine: `Vec<MachineView>`, each online machine with the summary it last reported, for
`orchestrator_capabilities`.

From a machine: `placement::Placed`, the machine of the account that runs a heavy worker it
would start, by the account's placement policy. `repo` is the project's origin, `need` the
account and model the worker runs on, and `exclude` the machines that refused it already.
`PairCode`.
`NewInvite`: a single-use code that lets one person create their own account on this hub.
`Invites`: the hub's signup mode and the account's codes nobody has used yet.
`null`. The code stops working; an error when the account has no such unused code.
A signed-out app's connectors, moved to the account on its first sign-in.

slack_keys.description: Each Slack bot's token by bot id. `slack_key` stays the default bot's.
